transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because the doctor who did my insurance physical told me my weight was too low. Which, honestly, I think is a bit ridiculous because I just look lean to me. I mean, I'm a painting worker, right? So I'm always up and down ladders, stretching, reaching, working these really long days. You know, last week we were painting this old Victorian house over on Elm Street, and the trim on those places is just a nightmare. It took us three days just to prep the wood. The guy who owns it kept coming out and offering us lemonade, which was nice, but it had way too much sugar in it. I try to avoid sugary drinks, you know? But yeah, the insurance doctor made a whole big deal about my weight, so here I am.
Have you noticed any unintentional weight loss recently, or have you been losing weight without trying?

Without trying? Well, no, it's not like it's an accident. I mean, most days I just keep it to coffee, and maybe I'll grab a protein bar between paint jobs. I usually get those peanut butter ones, though honestly they kind of taste like cardboard. I buy them in bulk at Costco. Man, Costco was an absolute nightmare this past weekend, they completely moved the hardware section around and I spent twenty minutes just trying to find the right width of blue painter's tape. The guy working there didn't even know where it was. 

But anyway, yeah, coffee, a protein bar, and then just a really small dinner at night. Because eating a full meal just feels like it would slow me down, you know? Like, if you eat a big lunch, you get sluggish. And when you're thirty feet up on an aluminum extension ladder, you really can't afford to be sluggish. My coworker Dave had this massive meatball sub for lunch last Tuesday and got so sleepy he almost dropped a full gallon of primer on a client's brand new driveway. It would have been a total disaster. So yeah, I just keep things light so I can keep moving.
Have you been having any nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or stomach pain recently?

No, no, nothing like that. My stomach's been totally fine. Honestly, the only time my stomach ever bothers me is if I accidentally use that cheap solvent without a mask. We had this job last month—an interior gig for this lady who wanted her entire kitchen cabinets refinished, right? And the contractor, this guy named Mike who always tries to cut corners, bought this off-brand paint stripper. It smelled like pure ammonia and rotten eggs. I swear, just opening the can gave me a headache for two days. I told Mike, I said, "You can't expect us to work in a closed kitchen with this stuff, it's a hazard." But he wouldn't listen, said it was all he could find. I ended up having to buy my own respirator just to get through the week. But yeah, as far as just regular stomach pain or getting sick? No, I don't have any of that.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or weak lately, even after getting enough rest?

Tired? I mean, maybe a little at the end of the day, but nothing crazy. I sleep fine. Actually, I just got this new mattress pad, one of those memory foam ones? It's supposed to have this cooling gel layer in it because my apartment gets so incredibly hot in the summer. The landlord refuses to fix the central AC, so I've just got this one rinky-dink window unit in the living room that sounds like a jet engine taking off. I tried to fix it myself last weekend, took the whole front panel off and cleaned the filter, which was absolutely disgusting by the way. Looked like a sweater had grown on it. But yeah, I sleep okay once the noise drowns out the traffic. So no, I wouldn't say I'm unusually weak or anything. Just normal tired from working.
Do you ever feel like you don’t have enough energy to get through your workday, even though you’re used to being physically active?

Energy? No, I always get through the day fine. You kind of have to, right? I mean, especially with exterior jobs, you can't just stop halfway and take a nap. Like this week, we're doing this huge two-story Victorian over on Maple Avenue. Beautiful trim work, but the owner has these massive, overgrown rose bushes planted right up against the siding. It is a complete nightmare trying to set up the scaffolding without crushing them. The homeowner—this retired guy, really nice but super particular—came out like four times yesterday just to watch us place the ladder feet. I get it, he loves his garden, but it adds so much time to the setup. Plus, his golden retriever kept trying to run off with my clean drop cloths. We actually had to ask him to keep the dog inside just so we could get the primer on the lower half. But anyway, yeah, I don't really run out of energy. I just keep moving until the job's done.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite recently, like not feeling hungry even when it's time to eat?

Appetite? I mean, I guess I'm just not that hungry most of the time. Most days I just keep it to coffee, maybe I'll grab a protein bar between paint jobs, and then just a really small dinner. Eating a full meal just feels like it would totally slow me down, you know? Especially when you're up on a ladder all day. Speaking of ladders, I actually had to replace my aluminum extension ladder last week. The locking mechanism on the old one was starting to stick, and you do not want to mess around with a faulty lock when you're twenty feet up trying to cut in a roofline. I went down to the hardware store—the local one, not the big box place, because the guys at the local spot actually know what they're talking about. The guy working there, Dave, he's been there forever, he showed me this new fiberglass model. It's heavier, which is kind of a pain to load into the truck, but man, it is so much more stable. And it doesn't conduct electricity, which is great because on that Victorian job I was telling you about, there are these old power lines that run right near the second-story eaves. The homeowner swears they're dead, but I'm not taking any chances. But yeah, food-wise, I just don't really have the time or the stomach for big meals.
Have you ever had any medical conditions that affect your digestion or nutrient absorption, like Crohn's disease, celiac disease, or chronic diarrhea?

Medical conditions? No, I don't think so. I mean, my stomach gets a little upset sometimes, but I definitely don't have any of those diseases you mentioned. Never had any real issues with digestion or anything like that. Though, speaking of stomachs, I did get food poisoning once a few years back from this sketchy food truck that parked near a job site we were on. We were painting this massive commercial warehouse out by the interstate. The whole exterior was this awful, faded mustard yellow, and they wanted it updated to this sleek charcoal gray. It was a huge improvement, honestly. But anyway, this taco truck would roll up every day at noon, and one day I decided to grab a pork burrito. Huge mistake. I was out of commission for like three days. My boss was so mad because we were already behind schedule. The weather had been terrible—rained for a week straight—so we couldn't spray the exterior. You can't spray when it's wet or too windy, you know? The paint just won't adhere right, and then you've got peeling and flaking a year down the road, and the client is calling you back to fix it for free. I hate callback jobs. They just eat into your profit margin. But yeah, other than that burrito incident, my stomach's always been pretty solid. So no, no chronic conditions or anything.
Can you tell me more about your typical daily food intake and whether you've noticed any unintentional weight loss despite eating this way?

Food intake? Uh, I mean, like I said earlier, it's mostly just coffee in the morning, maybe a protein bar if I remember, and a small dinner. As for weight loss... I don't know, I haven't really been paying attention to the scale. My work pants are a little looser, I guess, but I just figured that's from sweating so much on the job. Speaking of sweating, we had to wear these full Tyvek suits on a job last month. We were stripping lead paint off this old farmhouse porch, and let me tell you, those suits do not breathe at all. It was like eighty-five degrees out, high humidity, and I was just baking inside that thing. You have to wear the respirator, the gloves, the whole nine yards, because lead dust is no joke. The EPA regulations on that stuff are incredibly strict now. You have to put down plastic everywhere, seal off the windows, and bag up all the debris in these specific heavy-duty trash bags. We had this one inspector drive by—just happened to be in the neighborhood—and he stopped to check our containment setup. Thank god my boss is a stickler for the rules, because the fines for messing up lead abatement can bankrupt a small company. Anyway, it took us three days just to prep the site before we even touched a scraper. But yeah, I haven't really noticed any major weight loss, just the pants fitting a bit different, probably from all the sweating.
Have you lost more than 10 pounds unintentionally in the last six months?

Ten pounds? Uh, I really couldn't tell you. I don't even own a bathroom scale, to be honest, so I haven't been keeping track of numbers or anything. The only time I even look at a scale these days is when we're mixing two-part epoxy. We did this garage floor last week—massive three-car garage for this guy who collects vintage cars. He had this gorgeous '69 Mustang, cherry red, just sitting out in the driveway while we worked. 

But anyway, with that commercial-grade floor epoxy, you have to measure part A and part B exactly by weight, not volume. If you get the ratio even a little bit wrong, the stuff just never cures right. It stays tacky forever, and then you get what we call hot tire pickup, where the car tires literally peel the coating right off the concrete when they back out. It is a total nightmare to fix because you basically have to rent a diamond grinder and grind the whole floor down to bare concrete again. So I was out there with this little digital scale, carefully weighing out the hardener for like two hours... but yeah, as for my own weight, I have no clue if it's been ten pounds or what. I just haven't checked.
Do you use alcohol or any recreational drugs regularly?

Alcohol or drugs? No, I don't mess with any of that. I mean, I might have a beer like once a year at a barbecue, but that's it. Nothing regular, definitely no drugs. You really can't be doing that stuff in my line of work anyway. You have to be sharp. Like, last month we were hired to paint the crown molding in this massive, old Victorian house. The ceilings were fourteen feet high, and we had to set up scaffolding in the living room because a regular A-frame ladder wouldn't cut it. 

Setting up scaffolding inside a finished house is so stressful. You've got these heavy metal frames, and you're trying not to dent the original hardwood floors or scrape the antique wallpaper they just paid a fortune to have shipped from England. We had to put down layers of moving blankets and Ram Board before we even brought the pieces inside. And then you're up there, balancing on these aluminum planks, trying to cut a perfectly straight line between the ceiling and the molding with a brush. If your hands are shaking because you were out drinking the night before, you're going to get paint on the ceiling, and touching up a flat white ceiling without it flashing—where you can see the shiny spot from the new paint—is nearly impossible. You usually have to roll the whole ceiling corner to corner just to fix one little mistake. So yeah, you need a steady hand. But anyway, no, I don't drink or do drugs.
Have you lost more than 10% of your body weight unintentionally in the last six months?

Ten percent? Uh, I mean, like I said, I don't really know what my weight even is, so I couldn't tell you if it's been ten percent or five percent or whatever. I just don't keep track of it like that. I guess the only time I really think about percentages is when we're mixing custom paint colors. 

You know, people think you just go to the hardware store and pick a swatch, but it's way more complicated if you're trying to match something existing. We had this lady last week who wanted us to touch up her kitchen cabinets, but she didn't have the original paint can. She just had this one little chipped drawer front. So we had to take it to the paint store, and they put it under this spectrophotometer thing to read the color. But the computer only gets it right like eighty percent of the time. The guy behind the counter had to keep tweaking the formula, adding like a drop of black here, a drop of yellow oxide there. It's crazy how much math goes into it, figuring out the exact percentages of tint for a gallon versus a quart. If you get it even a fraction of a percent off, the new paint will dry slightly darker, and on a flat surface like a cabinet door, it sticks out like a sore thumb. We ended up having to paint the whole row of upper cabinets just so it would blend right. But yeah, as for my own body weight, I really have no idea about the percentages. I just haven't been checking.
